The time overlap is a fact; every candidate requires human verification — nothing here is an accusation.

strety.eyebrow: deterministic join over the graph · every candidate requires human verification
strety.title: Vote collisions
strety.intro: Where a verified company role and a chamber vote touch in time. Each row below is a computed candidate: an MP cast a positional vote on a print amending a statute that governs the public-money channel of a company where the registry confirms they held a role on that day. The time overlap is a fact; whether the vote actually concerned that company's interest is NOT computed here and requires a human reviewer.
strety.unavailable: The data layer is unavailable in this environment — this page cannot say whether any candidates exist, and refuses to guess.
strety.unavailableNote: Candidates are re-derived from the live record on every request; nothing is cached as an accusation.
strety.sources: sources: kg money layer (pass {pass}) · psp.cz roll calls (vote_event/vote_ballot, PSP10) · amends edges of the legislation layer · rule {rule}

rules.r1: Only ties that passed human review (verified), whose role the commercial registry confirms (ARES VR), and whose role period has a recorded start enter the join. A tie with no recorded review state counts as pending, never as verified.
rules.r2: A roll call enters only if it is not voided and links deterministically to a print: primarily through the session agenda (psp.cz bod_schuze — session + agenda item → print), as a fallback through a print number in its title. An agenda item covering several prints at once (joint debate) is conservatively skipped and counted separately — no candidate is ever built on an ambiguous key.
rules.r3: A print enters only if the graph records it amending at least one statute from the disclosed relevance table below, matched to the public-money channels that company actually has.
rules.r4: The vote day must lie inside the registry-confirmed role period — both boundary days inclusive.
rules.r5: Only a positional ballot (yes/no) forms a candidate; abstentions and absences never do.
rules.r6: One candidate per (tie × vote); several affected statutes merge into that one row.

strety.tableNote: The channel → statute table is fixed and printed verbatim above; it claims nothing about the substantive reach of any particular amendment. That is exactly why every candidate requires human verification.
strety.agendaNote: The session agenda dump (schuze.zip) is unavailable in this environment — only the title fallback links votes to prints here, so the linked count is a floor, not the record.
strety.pendingNote: {pending} registry-confirmed tie(s) with a recorded role period are still awaiting human review and would enter the join once verified; {noPeriod} verified tie(s) stay out solely because the registry period is missing. Neither group produces candidates here.
strety.emptyGate: No tie currently clears the join's entry gate — so there are zero candidates, honestly, not because nothing was checked.
strety.emptyGateNote: The gate requires human review + registry confirmation + a recorded role period (rule 1 above). The queue for reviewers lives at /penize/kontrola.
strety.emptyResult: The join ran over every eligible tie and the full roll-call ledger and found no time overlap that satisfies the rule. Zero is the result, not a gap.
strety.sentence: {name}{club} voted {choice} on print {bill} — “{billTitle}” — which amends {statutes}. On the vote day the commercial registry records the role “{role}” at {company} (IČO {ico}).
strety.overlapNote: The time overlap is computed; the substantive link is not established here and must be assessed by a human reviewer.

collisions.title: Print collisions
collisions.introReal: Two or more concurrently pending prints sometimes independently amend the same section of the same act in incompatible or order-sensitive ways. That is an ordinary hazard of bills drafted in parallel, not evidence of wrongdoing — a finding about the legislative process, not an ethical finding.

collisions.emptyData: The graph or the manual text-comparison outputs (stored in the analysis archive) are unavailable. Politicas does not display fabricated data.

collisions.clustersFootnote: A cluster = one § of one act, not a pair of prints — several findings are genuinely N-way (e.g. §35c of act 586/1992 now joins 4 prints). The classification is a derived finding (fabrication-checked; method: a deterministic same-section prefilter followed by a close read of both texts with in-text verification), never proven wrongdoing — it is a legislative-coordination risk between concurrently filed bills, not an ethical finding.

dependency.title: Dependencies on companion prints
dependency.aside: {billsFmt} prints · {hitsFmt} dependency findings · print texts on psp.cz
dependency.intro: The detector walks each print’s own text looking for the e-Sbírka drafting placeholder (“zákona č. …/2026 Sb.”), which a drafter inserts into amending sentences before the final act number is known. Each hit falls into one of three classes — the print cites its own later act, the print relies on ANOTHER, companion print that must pass at the same time or earlier, or the hit remains unclear because the available text carries no evidence for either of the first two. The classification was manually audited; even so, {unclearFmt} of {totalFmt} hits honestly remain unclear and are not rendered below. A dependency on a companion print is a fact of the legislative process — it flags an enactment-order risk (this print assumes the companion print will already be law), not an accusation of wrongdoing.
dependency.hitBadge: derived · awaiting review — a lead to examine, not a finding

record.heroNote: real data · psp.cz — PSP10 roll-call votes · lines, discipline and rebellions computed deterministically from stored ballots
record.lead: The Chamber's actual record: a cohesion seismograph over every valid roll-call vote, a ledger with a view onto the chamber floor, group lines and a chronicle of rebellions — every number links to psp.cz.
record.seismoNote: chamber cohesion over time · downward swing = splits · red = rebellion
record.seismoExplainer: Each column is one voting day. The deflection below the axis shows how much the groups split that day (100 % = all groups united); red spikes above the axis count ballots cast against a member's own group line. Pick a day for detail.
record.seismoAria: Chamber cohesion seismograph by voting day
record.seismoWorst: tightest day — the lowest cohesion sat at
record.ledgerNote: bar = chamber floor: cobalt for · ochre abstained/did not vote · gray not signed in · red against
record.ledgerFootnote: the ledger shows the {window} most recent of {valid} valid roll-call votes — the seismograph above covers them all · permanent link: pick an entry and share the address with #h-…
record.splitNote: breakdown by group — arrow = line (strict majority of positional ballots) · number = discipline
record.voteRebelsNote: voted against their own group line
record.noRebelsInVote: Nobody voted against their own group line.
record.disciplineNote: discipline and cohesion of the groups across all {valid} valid roll-call votes
record.matrixNote: line matrix — the ledger's 12 most recent roll-call votes
record.matrixFootnote: An outline instead of solid color means the group split (discipline below 90 %) — exactly where the Independence pillar begins. Dash: the group had no line (a tie of positional ballots, or nobody voted for/against).
record.chronicleNote: chronicle of rebellions — the {cap} most recent ballots cast against a member's own group line
record.noRebellions: No rebellion in the record yet.
record.topRebelsNote: rebellion rate — share of ballots against the line out of positional roll calls where the group had a line · only MPs with ≥ {minEligible} such votes
record.topRebelsEmpty: No MP has crossed the measurability threshold yet.
record.methodBody: Group line = strict majority of the group's positional ballots (for/against) in a given roll call; a tie determines no line. Discipline = share of the group's positional ballots on the line. Cohesion = the Rice index |for−against|/(for+against), weighted at chamber level by the positional-ballot counts of groups with ≥ 5 positional ballots. Since amendment 90/1995 Coll. the Chamber does not distinguish the “abstained / did not vote” slot and it does not count as a position; voided roll calls are excluded; unaffiliated MPs are displayed but not scored. The left-to-right ordering of groups in the hemicycle is an editorial constant.
record.methodSource: psp.cz — PSP10 roll-call votes · {valid} valid roll calls ({voided} voided excluded) · {ballots} ballots · {from} – {to}

kompas.heroNote: real data · psp.cz — PSP10 roll-call votes · questions picked by a disclosed rule, matches computed from actual ballots
kompas.title: Election compass, inverted
kompas.lead: Ordinary election calculators measure promises. This compass measures deeds: you take positions on real roll-call votes of the Chamber — and from the stored ballots it deterministically computes which MPs and groups voted like you. Every number links to the vote record.
kompas.howTo: FOR means voting for the motion exactly as it was put to the floor (the name is the literal vote title from psp.cz); AGAINST means voting against it. Skip a question you have no opinion on — it does not enter the computation.
kompas.questionsNote: {n} real roll-call votes picked by a disclosed rule — no editorializing
kompas.resultsNote: your result — cobalt marks your numbers, not published ones · the link carries it along
kompas.needMore: Answer at least {min} questions — {answered} so far. The result will appear here.
kompas.yourResultBadge: your result · computed from {answered} answered questions
kompas.clubsBoardNote: group line = strict majority of its positional ballots in a given roll call; a tie determines no line
kompas.mpsBoardNote: sorted by match; order within the same match carries only the count of comparable votes and the Czech alphabet
kompas.unrankedTail: {n} MPs have a positional ballot on fewer than half of your questions — shown below the line, unranked
kompas.selectionRule: Question selection rule: candidates are valid (non-voided) PSP10 roll-call votes with a theme from the vote_tag silver layer, excluding the Procedure and Other themes, with at least {minPositional} positional ballots (for + against). Within each theme, candidates are sorted by closeness |for−against|/(for+against) ascending (most divided first; ties: more positional ballots, more recent date, higher id). Themes are sorted by candidate count and the set is drawn round-robin — each theme's first pick, then the second — at most {perTheme} per theme and {cap} in total. The same record always yields the same questions.
kompas.scoringRule: Match rule: a roll call is comparable where the MP voted for/against; a match = their position equals yours. An MP's match = matches ÷ comparable votes. Since amendment 90/1995 Coll. the Chamber does not distinguish the “abstained / did not vote” slot — it counts neither as agreement nor disagreement and does not enter the denominator; absence does not either (both are shown separately). Only MPs with a positional ballot on at least half of your answered questions enter the ranking. Groups are measured the same way against their line (strict majority of the group's positional ballots).
kompas.rulesSource: psp.cz — PSP10 roll-call votes · {valid} valid roll calls, of which {tagged} themed and {candidates} selection candidates · {from} – {to} · themes: sem_classify (haiku), silver layer
kompas.entryBody: take positions on real roll-call votes and compute your match with MPs and groups
